lens: Whether every identifier the manuscript and its build artifacts print resolves to a real record — and specifically whether each PMID/DOI/PMCID supports the sentence that cites it, rather than merely existing. Check the deposit chain: that the archive manifest's recorded revision is a commit on origin, that its clean flag is honest, that the DOI the paper cites resolves to the record the repository believes it does, and that the preprint checklist's declaration of deposit drift matches what the manifest and the published record actually differ by.
what_i_read: PubMed E-utilities metadata for all 24 cited PMIDs, and the PMC full text of PMC12504171 (PMID 41055792)
central_claim: Two named 16-mer 5-6-5 gapmers across the two most-reported NR4A3 fusion junctions are the best designs a uniform five-screen in-silico specificity panel over 190 junction-spanning designs yields, the discriminating liability is the design's own wild-type parent rather than the transcriptome at large, and the ranking is falsifiable by a pre-registrable isogenic knockdown experiment whose selectivity threshold, replicate count and void condition are stated in advance.

p1s.summary: The cover letter's live status banner — the one non-superseded block in a document `submission_packet.py` lists as a required submission item — names a superseded, never-published DOI as the one 'both papers now cite' and states that the papers' archive links 'resolve to nothing'. Both halves are false at the pin.
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-cover-letter.md:25-41 is the file's only status block not wrapped in a '⚠ *Superseded, retained (rule 1.2)*' marker (the four that follow it, at :43, :50, :61, :68, all are). It reads: 'Both papers now cite **10.5281/zenodo.22180100**, a RESERVED BUT UNPUBLISHED version ... Until it is published the archive links in both papers resolve to nothing.' Re-derived against the pin: (a) WHICH DOI THE PAPERS CITE — `grep -n 'zenodo\.[0-9]*'` over the deliverables returns 10.5281/zenodo.22229096 and nothing else at fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md:411, fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md:2602 and :2757, fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv:38 and .fasta:37; pdfminer over the three built PDFs returns the single token 'zenodo.22229096' in the journal-article and preprint builds (the anonymized build correctly carries none). 22180100 appears in NO deliverable. (b) WHETHER IT RESOLVES — GitHub Actions run 33560898366, job 100032854734, `zenodo_verify.py` against the public records API, verbatim: 'record 22229096 — 10.5281/zenodo.22229096', 'state : done (submitted=True)', 'published : 2026-09-01', 'type : dataset', 'files : 1 emc-aso-archive.zip 8808345 bytes md5:957ae067bc96c964', 'PUBLISHED. The DOI both papers cite resolves to this record.' That matches deposit-state.json `published.doi`/`published.published` exactly. Direct resolution could not be attempted from this sandbox (doi.org and zenodo.org are both EGRESS_BLOCKED at the proxy), so the Actions log is the reading. Nothing binds the cover letter's identifier: `lint_citations.py` exits 0 with the stale DOI present (it anchors identifiers to a fetch, and 22180100 is anchored by deposit-state.json's superseded-versions list; currency is not one of its axes), and no test under research/manuscripts/tests or scripts/tests names the cover letter together with a DOI or 'zenodo'.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: The regression already happened and is silent by construction: this sentence turns over every time a new archive version is minted, and the file itself records that it has turned over three times before ('the third time this sentence has turned over on a new identifier'). Any future repoint of `deposition_doi` moves the papers, the sequence files, the manifest and deposit-state — all of which are checked — and leaves this banner untouched, because it is the only site of that identifier with no producing artifact and no guard. Fixing it by hand fixes only this turn; the fix that holds is to generate the banner from deposit-state.json, or to add a guard that the cover letter names no zenodo DOI other than the current `deposition_doi`.

p2s.summary: The manifest's drifted-promise gap — the check that fails the build when the archive keeps a commitment the paper has dropped — reads only the extended report. The condensed journal article's own Data availability sentence is outside the set it can see.
p2s.evidence: research/manuscripts/aso_archive_manifest.py:72 sets `PAPER = os.path.join(ASO, "fusion-junction-aso-research-article.md")`, and that single path is what every row's `_promise_still_in_manuscript` flag and therefore `gaps.promises_whose_sentence_is_no_longer_in_the_manuscript` is computed against; `main()` exits non-zero on a non-empty drifted list. The journal article's promise at research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md:409-412 ('All code, graded artefacts, per-design tables, every screen's parameters and the complete bounds on each claim are deposited under [doi:10.5281/zenodo.22229096] ... the citable record for them') is quoted by no row: of the 29 promise rows, 13 carry `_promise_still_in_manuscript: true` and the rest are labelled 'n/a — descriptive label, not a quotation', and every quoted fragment I could match resolves into the research article. CORRECT AT THE PIN — I ran `python3 research/manuscripts/aso_archive_manifest.py --check-archive` (exit 0, 'manifest inventory is current') and read `gaps`: `promises_resolving_to_no_file: []` and `promises_whose_sentence_is_no_longer_in_the_manuscript: []`, and each clause of the journal article's sentence maps onto a row that does resolve (reproduction_command, graded_rescores, per_design_tables, correction_record, where_each_number_lives). ⚠ LEAKAGE DISCLOSURE: while grepping repo-wide for RRID provenance, `grep -rn 'CVCL_C6MX|CVCL_C6MY' research/` returned matching LINES from four research/autonomy/review-seats/*.json files, which are on the may-not-read list. What I saw included prior seats' finding text about RRIDs being outside lint_citations' identifier classes, a 23-vs-24 reference count, and one phrase, 'the journal article's own availability promise unmapped', which overlaps this p2. I re-derived this item end to end afterwards from aso_archive_manifest.py:72 and the promise rows alone, with every later search scoped away from research/autonomy; the RRID verification below and every other finding here was derived before or independently of that grep.
p2s.what_edit_would_break_it: Rewording or narrowing the journal article's Data availability sentence — for example dropping 'every screen's parameters' or naming a file the archive no longer carries — would leave `gaps` empty and the manifest exiting 0, because the checker never reads that file. The condensed article is the paper a journal receives, so its availability promise is the one an outside reader tests.

p2s.summary: A second, typed drift figure survives in the checklist's now-closed §3-vi, in the present tense and against an unnamed baseline, 144 lines below the generated figure that supersedes it. The two disagree (17 vs 18) and the guard cannot see the older one.
p2s.evidence: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-preprint-checklist.md:608 reads '**The drift against the published record is now 17 deposited paths, all changed, none added or removed.**' inside '### 3-vi · ✅ CLOSED' (:523), which carries no 'Superseded, retained' marker. The live figure is at :464 in the generated block under '### 3-vii · ⛔ OPEN' (:445): '⛔ **18 paths changed, 0 added, 0 removed** against the published record's own manifest at `4fd4698daec0`'. I RE-DERIVED THE 18 INDEPENDENTLY: `git show 4fd4698daec0:research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-archive-manifest.json`, joined path->sha256 against the manifest on disk, gives added 0, removed 0, changed 18, and the 18 paths are exactly the 18 the generated block lists. `python3 research/manuscripts/aso_deposit_drift.py --check` exits 0. The 17 was a measurement against the PREVIOUS published record (22182180) taken while 22229096 was still an unpublished draft, so it was true when written; what makes it a defect now is that it is present-tense, names no baseline, and sits in a section headed CLOSED whose neighbouring sentences ('⛔ IT IS NOT PUBLISHED AND MUST BE REFRESHED FIRST') are also no longer true. `test_a_declared_drift_states_the_size_it_actually_has` cannot reach it: `_drift_item` narrows to the generated block inside §3-vii, deliberately and for a documented reason.
p2s.what_edit_would_break_it: Nothing breaks it further — it is already stale, and the mechanism that keeps the §3-vii figure honest is precisely the mechanism that makes this one invisible. A reader searching the checklist for the drift size finds two answers and no way to tell which is current; the file's own §3-vii header argues that a typed size is not a number a human can maintain, and :608 is the counter-example still standing.

p2s.summary: The published archive the Declarations send a laboratory to for the orderable sequences is 18 paths behind the pin, and one of those paths is the sequence CSV itself. Already declared OPEN by the repository; what I add is the independent re-derivation and the named reader-facing consequence.
p2s.evidence: The manuscript's Declarations (research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md:389) say 'Order from the canonical record, `fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv`', and Data availability (:409-412) names 10.5281/zenodo.22229096 as where it lives. That record was uploaded at 4fd4698daec0 — GitHub Actions run 33560575257, job 100031800161, head_sha 4fd4698daec0c39ac77544083dc35d053a4e1e7e, log: 'updating existing draft 22229096 ... uploaded emc-aso-archive.zip' — and `fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv` is one of the 18 paths whose sha256 has since moved. Per the checklist's own §3-vii the CSV moved because 'the two `predicted_tm_*` columns are now documented as **not** the melting temperature of the reagent a laboratory would order', and the checklist states 'NOTHING PUBLISHED IS FALSE IN A WAY A READER ACTS ON WRONGLY EXCEPT THE Tm COLUMNS'. ⭐ WHAT LIMITS THIS, AND IT IS THE POINT WORTH RECORDING: `research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md` is byte-identical at 4fd4698daec0, 43d343fdd, d0b529cda and the pin (sha256 afd60b9ef7f3… at all four), so the deposited copy of THIS paper is the paper under review, and the paper's own Methods already carries the caveat the deposited CSV lacks ('Melting temperatures are nearest-neighbour values for an unmodified DNA:RNA hybrid at 250 nM strand ... so no absolute melting point is reported'). A reader who reads the paper is warned; a reader who opens the deposited CSV on its own is not. No blocker is claimed and no action is proposed here — §3-vii already owns the redeposit and gates it on a clean round.
p2s.what_edit_would_break_it: The size is a function of 515 deposited paths, so any commit anywhere in the repository can move it without the author knowing the archive exists — which is why §3-vii generates it. The risk this row names is the opposite one: that a future session reads 'the manuscript is byte-identical' and concludes the deposit is current, when the reader-facing file the Declarations point at is not.
